lesson: Use actual public fingertip side-contact geometry, not the nominal grasp TCP, for a top-down wrist and controlled tile-toppling arc.
Use an unoccluded current image for each topple check. A shared arm and high lateral withdrawal avoid unnecessary wrist rotations between adjacent targets.
Monocular rectangle scale alone gave unstable stock height. Use current visible layer count and image-measured tile thickness, then verify the small lift visually.
A supported replacement can expose a plain green face, not only a white inset. Re-localize it after release instead of replaying the donor target.
Compute table release clearance from the complete padded public finger envelope, not only the physical tip.
For an upright diagonal regrasp, derive the turn from the observed long axis. Split the half turn and check every sampled joint increment to avoid a near2pi IK branch jump.
Visual checks and completed waypoints are not official success. Only original native results establish qualification; small-sample success does not establish full benchmark reliability.
